refuted.claim: Apple explicitly directs designers to support combined-input interactions rather than designing for one input mode at a time.

Apple states that on iPad the pointing device is additive rather than substitutive — it does not replace touch — and requires that an app deliver an equivalent experience across gestures, pointer, and keyboard, meaning pointer-only interactions cannot be the sole path to a function.

Apple names the specific set of non-full-screen configurations an iPad app must be tested in: full screen, Split View, Slide Over, Picture in Picture, and dynamic resizing on an external display under Stage Manager.

Apple states that on iPadOS, designers should NOT build custom keyboard navigation for standard controls (buttons, segmented controls, switches) — Full Keyboard Access is the designated mechanism for control activation and gesture-based interactions like drag and drop; app-level keyboard navigation is scoped to text fields, text views, sidebars, and collection/custom views.
